sentences.text: 13.09.2023 Issue notice, making it returnable on 16.10.2023.

2. Mr. B. Gogoi, the learned counsel appears on behalf of the respondent No.1; Mr. A. Bhattacharjee,
the learned counsel appears on behalf of the respondent No.2; Mr. J. Chutia, the learned counsel appears on behalf of the respondent Nos.3, 4, 5, 7 & 8; Mr. J. Handique, the learned counsel appears on behalf of the respondent No.6 as well as Mr. C. Baruah, the learned counsel appears on behalf of the respondent No.9.
As the said counsels accept notice on behalf of the respondent Nos.1 to 9, extra copies of the writ petition be served upon them by 15.09.2023.
3. As regards the respondent Nos.10 to 13, the petitioners are directed to take steps upon them by way of registered post with A/D as well as through usual process by 15.09.2023.

4. The petitioners are further directed to take steps by way of dasti routed through the Registry of this Court upon the respondent Nos.10 to 13 and file an affidavit of service on or before the next date.

5. The petitioners herein have assailed the order dated 19.04.2023 passed by the Commissioner of Central Assam Division who is also the Page No.# 5/6 Arbitrator in terms with Section 3G of the National Highways Act, 1956.

The said order was passed in Case No.RR(CAD) 14/2023 on an application filed under Sub-Section (5) of Section 3G of the National Highways Act, 1956 by the private respondent Nos.10 to 13.
6.
This Court has perused the said application which has been enclosed as Anenxure-1 to the writ petition.

A perusal of the said application shows that the private respondents are aggrieved at the inadequacy of the compensation awarded by the competent authority, and as such, had filed the said application seeking enhancement of the compensation amount.

7. Taking into account that the reference made to the Arbitrator in question is only limited to the question of determination of the just and fair compensation on the basis of the well settled principles of law, the learned Arbitrator, in the opinion of this Court, ought not to have passed a direction to that effect that the respondents should not demolish the residential houses, structures and trees on the land covered by Dag No.203 of Khiraj Myadi Patta No.63.
More so, when by virtue of notification issued under Section 3D of the National Highways Act, 1956, the said property has already been vested upon the National Highway Authorities.

8. This Court further takes note of that in view of the said order dated 19.04.2023, the work to be carried out for four laning of the National Highway No.29 have been affected which hampers the Page No.# 1/6 vs The State Of Assam And 12 Ors on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107223598/
4 public interest.

9. Taking into account the above, this Court, therefore stays the impugned order dated 19.04.2023 passed in Case No.RR(CAD) 14/2023 only to the extent wherein there is a direction upon the respondents not Page No.# 6/6 to demolish the residential houses, structures and tress on the land covered by Dag No.203 and Khiraji Myadi Patta No.63 of the private respondents.

10. Another very relevant aspect of the matter arises for consideration for which the petitioners have been compelled to approach this Court is in view of a notification issued by the Principal Secretary to the Government of Assam, General Administration Department whereby the post of the Divisional Commissioner has been abolished and consequently there is no Arbitrator to adjudicate the case bearing No.RR(CAD) 14/2023.
11.

Mr. B. Gogoi, the learned counsel appearing behalf of the respondent No.1 submits that there is a move on the part of the concerned respondent authorities to entrust an official from the revenue Department for the purpose of execising the power of the Arbitrator in terms with Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.

Mr. B. Gogoi, the learned counsel on the next returnable date shall apprise this Court as to whether any official of Revenue Department has been entrusted to function as the Arbitrator in respect to those arbitration proceedings which arises out of the reference made under Section 3G (5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
12. List accordingly.
